metadata.case_name: LEE HAU MAN v. HON PING WAN

plaintiff.occupation_before: odd job worker in a shop

injuries.description: One was of the femoral neck
source: He had two fractures of the right Femur (bone of the thigh). One was of the femoral neck and the other of the shaft of the bone.

injuries.description: Fracture of the shaft of the right femur
source: He had two fractures of the right Femur (bone of the thigh). One was of the femoral neck and the other of the shaft of the bone.
On 30.5.78 the fracture of the shaft was treated by operation and the insertion of a bone plate and bone screw.

injuries.description: Possibility of osteo-arthritis in the right hip joint (post-traumatic)
source: there is a possibility of osteo-arthritis in the plaintiff's hip joint which is slightly disorganized by the presence of abnormal bone.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the hip or thigh

manifestations.description: Pain and aching in the region
3/8ths of an inch of shortening of the leg
Severe muscle wasting of the thigh muscles; the circumference of the right thigh is 12¼ and of the left, 14ins.
A neat, 8ins. operation scar on the outside of the right thigh.

Movements of the leg at the hip are severely restricted; can only bend the leg at the hip through 110° (normal 150°); deficit of 10° of internal rotation and limit of external rotation is 30° so instead of 75° of the combined movements he only has 20°.
Unable to completely straighten the leg at the knee joint, there being a deficit of 10° (reduced to 2–3° on later examination).
Used two sticks for four months and still uses one stick when outside the house but when inside he has to support himself on articles of furniture.
Takes 10 to 15 minutes to climb the stairs and he has to rest three or four times on the way up.
He is totally incapable of any form of work.

Impairment figures: a 4% Impairment of the leg from the knee; a 7% from loss of flexion of the hip and 15% from loss of rotation of the hip, making a 26% Impairment of the leg which is a 10% Impairment of the Whole Man (first report).
Overall Impairment is now 23% of the leg and a 9% Impairment of the Whole Man (second report).
Possibility of osteo-arthritis in the hip; pain and aching in the region would increase over 5–6 years.

treatments_received: Taken to Tang Shiu Kin Hospital and transferred to the Queen Mary Hospital
Traction with pin through the tibia below the knee
Operation on 30.5.78 for fracture of the shaft with insertion of a bone plate and bone screw
Traction re-applied with another pin through the tibia
Transferred to Sandy Bay Hospital for two months

losses.description: It takes him 10 to 15 minutes to climb the stairs and he has to rest three or four times on the way up.
When inside he has to support himself on articles of furniture.
He is totally incapable of any form of work.
There is a neat, 8ins. operation scar on the outside of the right thigh.
He has undergone a good deal of pain and suffering and loss of amenities.

comparable_cases.injury_description: 71 year old woman fractured her tibia, fibula and wrist, she remained in hospital for 101 days during which time her leg and wrist were in plaster, and she finally suffered a permanent disability of a slight limp.

Compound fracture of the right knee cap, fractures of the right ankle, left hand, and 7th right rib, and lacerations of the left knee; operation for removal of bone fragments from the right knee and open reduction and screwing of the ankle; knee could not be straightened and had only 65° of movement instead of the normal 165°; ankle limited.
